cache/grow: While a model writes, its KV cache keeps a key and a value from every head, for every token so far, at every layer. The longer the text, the more memory it takes.
cache/mha: With four heads, each eight numbers wide, one token costs two times four times eight: sixty four numbers per layer.
cache/mqa: The first fix was to share. In 2019, Noam Shazeer had every head read one key and one value: multi-query attention. The cache drops to sixteen numbers, at some cost in quality.
cache/gqa: In 2023, Joshua Ainslie and colleagues took the middle road, grouped-query attention: one key and value per group of heads. With two groups, thirty two numbers, and quality close to multi-head.
cache/ask: Both save memory the same way: heads give up keys and values of their own. Could the cache shrink, with every head keeping its own?
cache/mla: In 2024, the DeepSeek V two paper did just that, with multi-head latent attention.
latent/idea: The idea: squeeze each token's vector, x, into a much shorter one, and cache only that. When attention runs, every head rebuilds its own key and value from it.
latent/latent: The short vector is the latent, c. Latent means hidden, from the Latin for lying hidden: nothing reads c itself, the heads only rebuild from it.
latent/down: One matrix makes it: W D K V. A matrix that turns a vector into one of a new length is called a projection, and this one projects down: D for down, K V for keys and values.
latent/dc: The latent's length is d c, here sixteen, and that is all the cache keeps: sixteen numbers per token, per layer.
latent/up: To rebuild, each head multiplies c by its own part of W U K, U for up, and gets its key: eight numbers made from sixteen.
latent/uv: Its part of W U V makes its value from the same c: one latent serves keys and values alike.
latent/own: Each head's parts are its own, so each head gets its own key and value: nothing is shared.
latent/count: And those matrices are weights, stored once with the model, not per token. So the cache is as small as multi-query attention's, yet no head shares.
shapes/rule: The shapes follow the rule for any matrix: a row for each number it makes, a column for each number it reads.
shapes/down: W D K V reads a token's d numbers and makes sixteen, so it is sixteen by d: d c by d.
shapes/head: One head's part of W U K reads the sixteen numbers of c and makes an eight-number key: eight by sixteen, d head by d c.
shapes/all: Stack all four heads' parts, and the whole W U K has four times eight rows: thirty two by sixteen. W U V has the same shape.
real/big: DeepSeek V two has a hundred and twenty eight heads, each a hundred and twenty eight wide. Multi-head attention would cache thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty eight numbers per token, per layer.
real/small: Its latent has five hundred twelve numbers, plus one small key of sixty four, shared by every head, that carries the token's position: five hundred seventy six in all.
real/ratio: That is about fifty seven times smaller. And each of its sixty layers keeps a cache like that, so the whole model stores sixty times as much.
real/paper: Its authors report a cache as small as grouped-query attention with only two and a quarter groups, yet better results than full multi-head attention.
